newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures plunge, all months limit-down.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures plunge, all months limit-down.

text.p: All months of Tokyo corn futures plunged by the daily 500 yen limit by the close on Monday, due to local investor sales, traders said.
The benchmark September contract was down 500 yen at 15,190 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 102,781 lots.

Active selling from individual investors emerged from the opening, traders said. Bearish sentiment spread as local investors expected the spot December contract of the CBOT corn futures to fall below $3 a bushel soon, they said.
The yen's fall against the dollar was not big enough to encourage investors to buy, the traders said.

The dollar jumped to its highest level in more than 2-1/2 years on Monday against the yen, following the weekend G7 meeting and due to an expectation that U.S. interest rates have nowhere to go but up.

Japanese traders said they will start buying U.S. corn and soybean this week, assuming the trans-Pacific freight rates will recover gradually. The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.01 per bushel at 0825 GMT, against $3.03-1/4 at Friday's close. The spot November of the CBOT soybean futures was at $7.76-1/2 at 0825 GMT, against $7.83-1/4 on Friday.
